items.text: VNE - Never Exceed Speed - Do not exceed this speed in any operation: 160 KIAS (184 MPH)
VNO - Max structural cruising speed - Do not exceed this speed except in smooth air and then only with caution: 128 KIAS (147 MPH)
VA - Maneuvering speed: 2300 Pounds - 97 KIAS (111 MPH); 1950 Pounds - 89 KIAS (102 MPH); 1600 Pounds - 80 KIAS (92 MPH)
VFE - Maximum flap extended speed: 85 KIAS (97 MPH)
Maximum window open speed: 158 KIAS (184 MPH)
VS - Stall speed (No Flaps): 47 KIAS (54 MPH)
VS0 - Stall speed in landing configuration: 41 KIAS (47 MPH)
VX - Best angle of climb: 59 KIAS (68 MPH)
VY - Best rate of climb: 73 KIAS (84 MPH)
Chandelles - Max Indicated Airspeed: 105 KIAS (120 MPH)
Lazy Eights - Max Indicated Airspeed: 105 KIAS (120 MPH)
Steep Turns - Max Indicated Airspeed: 95 KIAS (109 MPH)
Stalls (except whip stalls) - Use slow deceleration
Angle of Bank 0° - 0° Flaps: 47 KIAS (54 MPH); 40° Flaps: 41 KIAS (47 MPH)
Angle of Bank 30° - 0° Flaps: 51 KIAS (59 MPH); 40° Flaps: 44 KIAS (51 MPH)
Angle of Bank 45° - 0° Flaps: 56 KIAS (64 MPH); 40° Flaps: 49 KIAS (56 MPH)
Angle of Bank 60° - 0° Flaps: 66 KIAS (76 MPH); 40° Flaps: 58 KIAS (67 MPH)
1. If enough runway remaining to land
Fly runway heading to emergency landing site
1. Gain all the altitude you can! Pull back (gently) to use the aircraft's momentum to gain altitude until airspeed falls off to the optimum glide speed (65 KIAS - 75 MPH).
Trim the airplane for optimum glide speed

Find a suitable place to land and fly to it. If altitude and distance to selected site permit, try to set up a normal landing pattern. If that's not possible, take what you can get. Regardless of whether or not a full pattern can be set up, make sure the approach results in a landing parallel to any furrows in the selected field.

items.text: With ignition switch off and throttle closed, prime the engine four to ten strokes as the propeller is being turned by hand. Use heavy primer strokes for best atomization of fuel. If doing this by yourself, tie the plane down securely and set parking brake, in case engine starts. Treat propeller as if the ignition is on and engine could start. Leave primer charged and ready for a stroke.

items.response: PUMP TO FULL OPEN TWICE THEN RETURN TO 1/8 INCH OPEN POSITION
CONTINUE TO PRIME UNTIL ENGINE IS RUNNING SMOOTHLY. ALTERNATELY PUMP THROTTLE RAPIDLY OVER FIRST 1/4 OF TRAVEL

items.text: This might take a little time since the engine is cold. If pressure doesn't come up in about 30 seconds, shut the engine down.

items.response: FULL ON AFTER ENGINE STARTED. LEAVE ON UNTIL RUNNING SMOOTHLY

items.text: If engine does not start during the first few attempts, or if engine firing diminishes in strength, it is probable that the spark plugs have frosted over. Pre-heat must be used before another start is attempted.

Pumping the throttle may cause raw fuel to accumulate in the intake air duct, creating a fire hazard in the event of a back-fire. If this occurs, maintain a cranking action to suck flames into the engine. An outside attendant with a fire extinguisher is advised for cold starts without pre-heat.
Perform steps 3 through 5 on normal start checklist
Brief passengers on use of belts/harnesses and requirements for wearing them.

items.response: OFF (TAKE KEY OUT AND HANG IT UP)

items.text: With ignition switch off and throttle closed, prime the engine two to four strokes (up to seven without pre-heat) as the propeller is being turned by hand. Use heavy primer strokes for best atomization of fuel. If doing this by yourself, tie the plane down securely and set parking brake, in case engine starts. Treat propeller as if the ignition is on and engine could start.
This might take a little time since the engine is cold. If pressure doesn't come up in about 30 seconds, shut the engine down.
Perform steps 3 through 5 on normal start checklist
Set attitude indicator to level flight position. Set altimeter to runway altitude or locally reported altimeter setting. Set heading indicator to magnetic compass.
RPM drop should not exceed 125 RPM on either magneto. RPM difference between magnetos should not exceed 50 RPM.

items.text: Under light (less than 10 Knots) wind conditions 10° descending on the end of the downwind leg, 20° on base, and full flaps over the threshold. In heavier winds 20° or less is good flap setting for landing. Use minimum flap setting possible for cross wind landing.
Airspeeds: Downwind through base 65 - 75 KIAS (75 - 86 MPH); Final approach 60 - 70 KIAS (70 - 80 MPH); In gusty winds add 1/2 difference between gust and average wind speed to approach speed.
